notes: Seal of Fury, Holy Shield on cooldown, Holy Strike, Hammer of the Righteous and Judgement, with Consecration only on spare mana and the three defensives on low health. Righteous Fury is not a line: it is a request option (PaladinOptions.righteousFury), worth +60 percent threat on Holy damage and, with Improved Righteous Fury, up to 9 percent less damage taken. Devotion Aura is not a line either: the kit keeps it on (sim/leveling/kit.go), as the Protection paladin's own armor aura; Blessing of Sanctuary is not in this client. Judgement no longer consumes the seal in Forever (Blizzard's Deep Dive recap), so Seal of Fury is recast every 30 seconds rather than after each Judgement. Mana is the limiter, so every other spell leaves Holy Shield's cost (240 mana at rank 4, new at level 60 in client 1.60.1.70753; measured against rank 3 on the tank fight, raid and bare, 10,000 iterations, seeds 1 and 50001: about 8 percent more threat with raid buffs and 11 percent more bare, damage taken unchanged) in the pool: Holy Shield is both the best mitigation and the best use of mana. Holy Strike sits straight after Holy Shield because, with Iron Creed (in the guide build), it is mitigation as well as threat: while Righteous Fury is on it cuts the damage taken for 6 seconds, and Shieldsworn (client 1.60.1.70707, in the guide build) brings its cooldown down to 6 seconds and makes each strike fire Holy Shield's block damage and Shield Specialization's mana while Holy Shield is up. Swift Judgement is a second Judgement of the Seal on its own one minute cooldown since 1.60.1.70707, so it is cast whenever it is ready. Measured by hand on the engine's tank fight (spec-breakdown -tank with the published level 60 raid-ready set against the curated boss, 10,000 iterations; rotation-search scores damage only and skips tank specs), each line against the same rotation without it: Holy Shield 6 percent more damage taken and 21 percent less threat without it, Holy Strike 4 percent more damage taken and 7 percent less threat, Hammer of the Righteous 17 percent less threat, Consecration 12 percent less threat, Judgement 7 percent less threat. Moving Holy Strike ahead of Holy Shield, Hammer ahead of Holy Strike, Judgement ahead of Hammer, or Consecration's mana floor between 30 and 80 percent, moved nothing past the noise. The defensives on health (Templar's Bulwark below 35, Divine Shield below 25, Divine Protection below 20 percent) cut the chance of death on a boss that hits harder than the published one and rarely fire on it. Unconfirmed, and moving this list: Hammer of the Righteous as 3 times the main hand weapon's damage per second (the client's text; whether attack power counts is not stated), Consecration's damage as the client's companion rows state it (12 a second to everything in the area and 27 more to the first four, 0.095 spell power on the extra), and Divine Protection and Divine Shield under their Classic Era ids.

Below 25% health, once Forbearance from Templar's Bulwark has gone. Ten seconds immune, twelve from rank 2 at 50, at half damage dealt.

Dwarf: Stoneform when you drop under 70% health. Ten percent less physical damage for 8 seconds, on the global cooldown, every 3 minutes.
Keep it up and recast it in its last 2 seconds, and once you have Holy Shield at 30, only with its mana left over. Judgement does not consume it, so this is one cast every 30 seconds.
On cooldown. Its 10 second cooldown matches its duration, so it is up whenever its four charges last, and it is the first claim on your mana.

On cooldown. Strong threat for little mana, twenty mana at 60; with Iron Creed it also cuts your damage taken for 6 seconds, and from 40 Shieldsworn brings it back every 6 seconds. Always your newest rank: the flat Holy damage grows with each rank and is not reduced by the weapon-damage part of the strike.
On cooldown, once Holy Shield's mana is safe. It hits your target and up to three enemies next to it, for Holy damage that Righteous Fury multiplies, so it carries your threat on a pack.
Whenever it is ready. A second Judgement of your Seal on its own one minute cooldown, free and off the global cooldown; under Seal of Fury it taunts too, so hold it when a tank swap is coming.
On cooldown, and once you have Holy Shield at 30, only while its mana is safe. Off the global cooldown for 6% of base mana, and under Seal of Fury it is your taunt.
On Undead and Demons only, and once you have Holy Shield at 30, only while its mana is safe. It cannot be cast on anything else.

Last, while what you hold plus what you regain, less what you spend, over the rest of the fight still pays for it, or once you drop below 35% health. It spends only mana your strikes and, from 30, Holy Shield will not need, and from 40 Hammer of the Righteous makes far more threat for its mana. Rank 1 does a little more than rank 2 at 30 to 38 because it costs less and you can drop it far more often on a dungeon pull; your newest rank from 39, and rank 1 again at 60 without raid buffs.

expected_idle.reason: Holy Shield needs a shield and the ladder's character carries none (a paladin's off hand is a weapon slot only for dual-wielding classes), so the engine refuses the cast at every level. A tank in the tank fight, shield on, casts it every 10 seconds.

Exorcism only lands on Undead or Demon (sim/paladin/exorcism.go's ExtraCastCondition); the published tank boss, like the ladder's target, has no creature type, so this line's gate structurally can never pass against it.
